finding: P24 is scored 'between' but its registered refutation clause is met. The clause is 'at or below 1.7 percent (the row bootstrap value)'. The exact round 4 row bootstrap upper bound is 1.72035, and the cluster upper bound is the same 1.72035, so the cluster bound is at (not above) the row bootstrap value. The script compares against the rounded literal 1.7, which is the reading more favourable to the prediction. That breaks the rule stated in the scores header (use the less favourable reading and name it).
evidence: stats/results/cycle_cluster_bootstrap.csv row fitted / test, all: median_abs_cluster_ci_hi 1.72035, median_abs_row_ci_hi 1.72035, median_abs_round4_row_ci_hi 1.72035. Script line 112: verdict(hi >= 2.5, hi > 1.7). STATISTICS_V5 section 1.1 itself says 'The cluster interval is not wider at the top'.
suggested_fix: Compare against median_abs_round4_row_ci_hi rather than 1.7, score P24 as miss, name both readings in the evidence text, and update the totals (15 hit, 1 between, 11 miss) in the scores, RUN_LOG and any rubric or paper text that quotes them.

line_or_section: P6, P9 (also P7, P8, P10 to P13)
finding: The less favourable reading rule is not applied the same way everywhere. P6 (flights processed; refuted if fewer than 20) and P9 (completed missions per configuration; refuted if fewer than 10) are count metrics that can be computed, and both counts are 0. Read literally, both refutation clauses are met. The script marks them 'not scored' (tool or source unavailable) without naming the second reading, while P19, P21, P22 and P26 are pushed to the stricter reading.
evidence: Script lines 53-63 hard code 'not scored'. data and docs: no flight log downloaded (FLIGHTSTACK_STUDY section 4), no sitl/ results (MISSION_STUDY section 8: SITL skipped).
suggested_fix: Either score P6 and P9 as miss under the literal reading, or keep 'not scored' and state in the evidence text that the literal count reading (0) would give a miss. Apply one documented rule to every prediction.

finding: The P21 miss rests on firmware_counter_unsigned_version. That model variant is weaker than the design and was not in the registered clause. The stated firmware design already signs the image and its version (FORMAL_VERIFICATION F3: 'Stated design (signature over image and version, no counter)'), so 'the stated design plus a counter' is firmware_fixed_counter, which is proved, while the no counter model gives a counterexample. That is exactly the registered prediction. The score treats an added variant as a reading of the clause and does not name the alternative reading (hit).
evidence: formal/results/proverif_results.csv D1: firmware_stated_no_counter counterexample; firmware_fixed_counter proved; firmware_counter_unsigned_version counterexample. Script: 'miss' if 'counterexample' in [fixed_counter, unsigned_version].
suggested_fix: Name both readings in the evidence text (stated design plus counter: hit; any counter design including an unsigned version: miss), and say that the unsigned version model was written after registration. Keep the stricter verdict only if the protocol's rule says so explicitly.

finding: P35 is scored 'hit' by a string test ("LMS" in the text and "session" in the lowercased text) that cannot fail in practice, so the verdict is not computed from any rerun. The registered refutation is that either design changes. In this round the command design did change (a vehicle ML-DSA-44 signature, a fourth flight and key confirmation, F1), and so did the firmware design (signed version plus monotonic counter, F3). The evidence text even says 'now with the vehicle signature'. Under the less favourable reading this is a miss or between, and the reading is not named.
evidence: docs/REFERENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 1 items 1 and 2 (F1 and F3 adopted); script line 161 unchanged = ('LMS' in ra) and ('session' in ra.lower()).
suggested_fix: Score from a structured field (for example the recommended architecture letters and primitives written by mission/run_all.py). State both readings: primitive family unchanged (hit) against design changed by F1 and F3 (miss). Apply the less favourable one or explain why not.

finding: P25 is scored 'between' (compiler largest) from the main unweighted fit only. In that fit the compiler share (50.1 percent) and the statistic share (39.4 percent) have the same interval, 0.0 to 87.4 percent, so the largest factor is not identified. In the fit without the 12 worst observed rows, statistic is largest (36.9 percent), which meets the refutation clause ('source or statistic'). The less favourable reading is not used or named. Also, the 'statistic' factor is a regular expression classifier in which 'other' (87 rows) mixes 'not stated' with worst case, and compiler 'not stated' is one level holding 204 of 408 rows. Both factors therefore partly encode reporting practice, not the statistic or compiler.
evidence: data/meta/hierarchical_variance.csv: main unweighted statistic share 0.39365 (CI 3.1e-07 to 0.874), compiler 0.500948 (CI 9.5e-08 to 0.874); worst observed rows excluded: statistic 0.368596, variant 0.324611, compiler 0.157795. stats/meta_hierarchical.py statistic_of and compiler_of.
suggested_fix: Name both readings in the P25 evidence. Report the top factor as not identified when the intervals overlap fully. In STATISTICS_V5 and PAPER 4.1, describe the statistic and compiler factors as 'stated statistic or not stated' and 'stated compiler or not stated'.

line_or_section: Section 5, Hybrid handshake under the EU868 duty cycle
finding: The document disagrees with the data files it cites. It says the flights come from linksim/results/protocols_flights.csv and the protocol simulation column from linksim/results/protocols_grid.csv (handshake_mean_s at zero loss). Both files now hold the four flight handshake of F1. The table instead shows the frozen three flight values. For mavlink2_pq hybrid it shows 9.23 h at DR0 and 16.6 min at DR5, while protocols_grid.csv gives 38961.3 s (10.8 h) and 1127.16 s. Nowhere in the study document is the reader told that the ns-3 runs and this comparison use the superseded handshake; only PAPER threat 9 says so.

suggested_fix: Change the netsim/make_study.py text to cite netsim/results/ns3_handshake_flights.csv and linksim_lora_flights.csv, and add a sentence that the comparison uses the round 4 three flight handshake, not the reference design. Either rerun ns-3 on the four flight handshake or label the rows as superseded.

finding: Table 1 says a 'proved' result means the 'property holds for unbounded sessions'. That does not hold for the firmware proof (D1, firmware_fixed_counter). That model has one vendor with three signed releases and devices that boot three times each, so it is a bounded proof. FORMAL_VERIFICATION section 1 states this bound, but the paper does not.
evidence: formal/models/firmware_fixed_counter.pv: Vendor emits img1 to img3 once; Device has three boots (Device plus Third). FORMAL_VERIFICATION.md line 15: 'each booting three times, with three signed releases'.
suggested_fix: Change the Table 1 meaning to 'holds for unbounded sessions (session and fallback models) or for unbounded devices with three releases and three boots each (firmware models)', or extend the firmware model to unbounded releases and boots.

line_or_section: PAPER 4.6 last sentence of first paragraph; STATISTICS_V5 section 3
finding: 'link outages, not cryptography, set availability' is stated as a finding, but the Sobol ranking mostly reflects ranges that were assumed. The outage rate (0 to 30 per hour) and the mean outage (1 to 30 s) are mission/study.py Morris bounds over labelled assumptions. Signature, key and ciphertext sizes are held fixed, and cryptography varies only through impl_factor (1 to 2.3), the X25519 cycles and the MAC cycles, while the compute share is at most 0.0024. The P27 'hit' is therefore close to true by construction.
evidence: STATISTICS_V5 section 3 inputs table and the 'Kept fixed' paragraph; REFERENCE_ARCHITECTURE section 3 compute share 0.0024; mission/assumptions.csv labels outage inputs as assumption.
suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence: 'within the assumed outage ranges and with message sizes fixed, the outage inputs carry most of the variance'. Add a sensitivity in which the sizes vary (for example ML-DSA-65 or a larger KEM) before claiming that cryptography does not matter.

finding: The headline fleet change in the abstract and the proposal pack, 0.201 to 0.300, uses the 'uncertain' threshold scenario. The registered P4 scenario is stack optimised, where the change is 0.186 to 0.398, and the abstract does not say which scenario its figure belongs to. Section 4.5 also gives 'interval 0.297 to 0.303'. That is a bootstrap interval of the median over 200 draws, not the spread of the share: round 4 reported the 2.5 to 97.5 percentile spread for the same scenario as 0.186 to 0.232. Presented as 'interval', it understates the uncertainty by about an order of magnitude.
evidence: planner/results/flightstack_mc_summary.csv rows stack_asm and uncertain; PAPER.md line 143 (round 4 percentile 0.186 to 0.232); PREDICTIONS_V5 P4 metric 'stack optimised thresholds'.
suggested_fix: Name the scenario in the abstract and the proposals (or give both scenarios). In 4.5, call 0.297 to 0.303 the 95 percent interval of the median and add the percentile spread of the share over draws.

line_or_section: PAPER abstract and 4.3; NETSIM gap verdict
finding: 'Any one of three unstated settings' and 'three single causes each bring ns-3 into that range' overstate two of the three causes. (a) For 16 neighbours only the mean lies in 30 to 60 s: its 95 percent interval is 18.98 to 47.44 s, and the follow up interval is 28.20 to 34.76 s, so part of the plausible range lies below 30 s. (b) macMinBE 8 is not a single setting change, because macMaxBE was also raised from 5 to 8 to allow it.
evidence: NETSIM_STUDY.md sections 4 (neighbours 16 row, follow up table) and the text 'macMinBE values above 5 are run with macMaxBE 8'.
suggested_fix: State that 16 neighbours reaches the range on the mean only, with an interval that crosses 30 s, and that the backoff cause sets macMinBE and macMaxBE to 8 together.

finding: 23 of 241 runs are excluded, and 20 of them are attributed to 'an artefact of the simulator at the pinned version, not radio behaviour'. No cited ns-3 issue, code reference or diagnostic run supports this. The exclusions fall in the high hop and high load cells, where ns-3 and linksim diverge most, so the claim affects which cells count as 'incomplete' rather than as evidence of collapse.
evidence: NETSIM_STUDY.md line 154; gap_sweep rows hops 5 and 6, 4 hops with 4 or 8 neighbours, 6 hops with any load.
suggested_fix: Cite the ns-3 code path or issue behind the BUSY_RX state, or reword as 'cause not established', and report the share of stuck runs per cell as a result.

line_or_section: MISSION 4.1 'unauthenticated' column; REFERENCE_ARCHITECTURE section 3 first bullet
finding: Architectures on the same link do not share random draws. The 'unauthenticated' availability of the same command stream varies by architecture: SiK drone 0.9912 to 0.9920, IEEE 802.15.4 drone 0.9909 to 0.9924. These spreads are as large as or larger than the confidence interval half widths. The B against A comparison (0.9914 against 0.9916) and the IEEE 802.15.4 ordering (B 0.9922 above A 0.9909) are therefore within draw noise, yet REFERENCE_ARCHITECTURE section 3 reads the difference as coming 'only' from the session start.
evidence: MISSION_STUDY.md 4.1 rows SiK A to D and IEEE 802.15.4 A to D, unauthenticated column.
suggested_fix: Use common random numbers across architectures for the same link and vehicle, or report each architecture's loss against its own unauthenticated baseline (paired difference with an interval).

line_or_section: Section 3, free memory given to the planner
finding: 'The smaller value where both stacks were built' is taken separately for flash and for RAM, so a board can get PX4 free flash with ArduPilot free RAM (Pixhawk 6C: 39.784 kB flash from PX4, 937.396 kB RAM from ArduPilot), which is a combination no build has. The RAM capacity definitions also differ between stacks (ArduPilot includes ITCM, PX4 excludes it). RAM never binds here (minimum 111 kB against a need of 62 kB), so the impact is nil, but the method text does not describe this.
evidence: planner/flightstack_study.py measured_free (pick applied per resource); planner/results/flightstack_free_used.csv.
suggested_fix: Say in the method text that the minimum is taken per resource, or take both values from the same stack.
